utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. I understand we're in closed session for a matter you wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution would like to raise a serious matter in relation to this witness. Through the Outreach Programme of the Tribunal, we have received information that the name of the witness was reported in the VIP Daily News Report. It's a Belgrade-based press agency. And we have prepared the document for everyone to be available. On page 5 of this Daily News Report, there is the item "The Hague Tribunal and the trial of Milosevic continued after the recess," and it reports about the open parts of the testimony that the witness gave. But then in the third-last paragraph, it says: "Peter Michael Mueller, legal representative of Witness C-036, who is, according to documents of Prosecution, accused himself and is soon to be indicted, is present as Witness C-061 giving evidence in the courtroom of The Hague Tribunal." And the last paragraph says: "Former officials of Krajina who are living in Belgrade say that it is possible that under the code of protected Witness C-061 is Milan Babic, Prime Minister of the SAO Krajina government at the time when these events happened." First of all, the Prosecution wants to state that there are no documents that the Prosecution is actually accusing this witness. The only documents that exist are the indictment, where the witness is mentioned as a co-perpetrator. And there was also this document, the conviction from the Croatian courts, that was discussed in private session. In addition to that, the status of the witness was also only discussed in private session. Therefore, the Prosecution is very much concerned and alarmed, because the Prosecution, of course, did not inform anyone outside of the Tribunal about the status of the witness. The Prosecution is not only alarmed but will also try to find out which reporting is actually the basis of the information in the press agency, because there must be a source for this information in the press agency, and we try to find out. But we wanted to put the Trial Chamber on notice of this problem. At the moment, there is only the speculation who the Witness C-036 is, and the Prosecution is determined to keep his identity hidden and would like to proceed in the way that we did before, that is, parts only in open session, and everything that relates to the identity of the witness in private session. The Prosecution hopes that this event does not discourage the witness to give testimony further on, and hope he's not scared to continue to tell the truth. This is what the Prosecution wanted to inform the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Investigation should continue, and when you have further to report, you can do so in closed session to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we concluded discussing a meeting, and we spoke about the unification, or the attempts of the unification of the two Krajinas and what was discussed. And just to conclude this, I would like to put two documents to you, and that is Exhibit 352, tab 46 and 47. Tab 46 is the contract on the cooperation concluded between the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina and the municipalities of Bosnian Krajina of the 24th of June, 1991; and tab 47 is the declaration of the unification of the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina and the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina of the 27th of June, 1991. We do not need to discuss this further. It's just -- can you authenticate that these are the documents, underlying documents, to the events that you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both these documents refer to the events that I have testified about, the contract on cooperation from Banja Luka, and a declaration on unification from Bosansko Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the unification, the second document, was then not signed, as we can see, by Mr. Kupresanin. Is that due to the intervention of Mr. Karadzic that you spoke about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Karadzic prohibited it. He even asked deputies from the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina to go back and to vote again against the declaration. However, they refused and they left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to put a third document to the witness in this context, and it's tab 45 of Exhibit 352, and it is a letter of Radovan Karadzic. And in this letter, it -- I quote: "Along with the congratulations, accept our assurances that the Bosnia and Herzegovina Serb National Council will always by the spiritual, cultural, political and state unity also mean state unity of the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina and all the other Serb regions with the Serbia mother-country within a free, democratic and federative Yugoslavia, regardless of its site -- size." Sorry, "size." We do not need to discuss this because it speaks for itself. Can you tell us -- there is no date on this document. Can you tell us when it was sent? Do you know that? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the 21st of December, 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that? Is it because of the congratulation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 21st of December was the date when the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina was proclaimed in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have yesterday spoken about the goal "all Serbs in one state," and you have testified about how Mr. Seselj understood it and what was supposed -- what was planned or what was not addressed in relation to the non-Serb population in this territory. What did you see happen on the ground to the non-Serb population in the SAOs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August 1991, the Yugoslav People's Army entered into the war with Croatia. The JNA engaged in combat operations in such a way that by moving the front line closer to the opposing party, using heavy artillery, it forced the population and members of the armed forces of the Croatian government and the entire population to withdraw and retreat from those territories. In this way, the JNA, as of August 1991, engaged in a war so that the territories that it captured would be left without any Croatian inhabitants, or very few of them. Houses and buildings were destroyed in the combat operations and subsequently. Property was looted. And in this way, JNA gained control of territory together with other armed formations that were within its ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which other armed formations do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were units of the Territorial Defence under the command of the Yugoslav People's Army and the militia or police of Krajina, as well as volunteer units, so-called volunteer units, under the control of a parallel structure of state security and the police of Krajina and units commanded by the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see such activities unfold? Can you give us the names of the location where you saw that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that in the area of Kijevo around Vrljika, the area around Drnis, the area around Obrovac, that is Maslinica, around Kostajnica, around Glina, Vidusevac, Petrinja, Slunj, and other places in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Kostajnica region, were the villages Dubica, Cerovljani, and Bacin attacked in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the region close to Plaski, were the villages Saborsko, Poljanak, and Lipovanic attacked in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the region near Knin, were Skabrnja, Nadin, and Bruska attacked in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these villages that I just mentioned, were these Croatian villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Croatian or majority Croatian villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these villages pose a threat to the JNA or the Serb people in the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that various formations were involved. Did they get involved in a certain pattern so that one formation went first, did something, and then others follow? Can you describe how these forms of attack actually were conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a rule, and that was that the first to take part in attacks were police units or volunteer units or units under the control of the State Security Service. They would engage in provocations, provocative shootings, individual opening of fire towards Croatian settlements, and then they would open fire with mortars. In other words, they would provoke the other side, upon which the JNA would join in with its artillery and all the units under its control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned state security. Which state security did you mean was involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the JNA had joined and attacked, what happened afterwards when a village was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, there was looting and torching of property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did this, which formations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done also by the JNA, while it held control, especially in Drnis. I know of a case there. And then the JNA would hand over control, or rather, it would leave the area without any control for a certain period of time. The police would not establish its control there and then the looting would become generalised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those -- you said that -- what did the Croatian population do when this attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone stay behind? Did any people stay behind, and if so, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few people stayed behind, mostly elderly people. After that, there would be individual killings, which in most cases would not be elucidated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were people also detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was detention as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detained people, were they mistreated in detention? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard stories that there was mistreatment of people in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisons actually established in Knin, and do you know whether people were mistreated there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two prisons in Knin. One was controlled by the police, and another by the JNA. I heard that there was mistreatment in the prison controlled by the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Towards the end of 1991/the beginning of 1992. I was told this by the Minister of Justice, Risto Matkovic. He was the first to tell me. And then later on, in 1992 and 1993, there was quite a lot of talk about this by ordinary people, and that was the reason why the Minister of Justice, Risto Matkovic, sought for the ministry to take over control of the prisons that were held by the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just clear up something. You said -- see if I can find it - after the population fled, some people stayed behind, mostly elderly. After that you said there would be individual killings, and then this: "... which in most cases would not be elucidated." Now, that's not clear. What did you mean by "elucidated"? It may be a translation problem, but perhaps you could just clarify it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That an investigation was not conducted to discover the perpetrator of the killing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to play now a few intercepts dealing with the matter, but I forgot to ask you something. Were people also -- those who stayed behind, these elderly that you said, were they also deported or forcibly transferred to other places outside of the control of this Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there were cases of individual local officials having to shelter these people, to protect them from people in the police or the state security so that they wouldn't kill them, but that this was not sufficient. And I was told of a group that they had to help leave the area under their control so that they could cross over into the territory under the control of the Croatian government. I heard this over the media, that there were large-scale deportations, such as the one in Ilok. I also heard stories that people from Kostajnica, Croats, left the town after the town had been captured by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that local officials had to shelter these people, and you mentioned in this context the police and the state security. They had to shelter them from the police and the state security. Is that the parallel structure again that you mentioned earlier on, around Milan Martic and Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the people linked to them and under their protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which official --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, we have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which official told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted), told me, after those events, when we arrived in Belgrade. He told me that he had to protect people from people who were under Frenki's protection, (redacted), to put them in a house, where he fed them, so that they wouldn't be killed by people within Frenki's circle, but that this was not sufficient, but that he had to escort them towards (redacted), that is, territory under the control of the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go now into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We want now to play a part of an intercept, and it's the Exhibit 353, tab 16. And we actually split this intercept into two parts: track 2 and track 3. First we play a part of this. It's track 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but it is impossible to follow this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can the transcript be put to the witness, the transcript? The sections played are marked in the transcript, and in the English it is also marked in the translation. Can we try it again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell the page number. I don't see any mark.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The first section that is played is on page 2, and it starts with "Where does he ..." and it ends with "You offered them what I would never offer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So that everybody can follow this, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, I think it may be an idea to put some foundations down. Perhaps you can deal with the witness. He heard the voices. Who do we have speaking on this tape, so that we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I actually wanted to let the witness hear it first. And as it is not possible to translate it, I don't think that it makes any sense to continue playing it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but they can't find the exact section.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually marked for you too, but ... Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, who is speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the speakers -- the voice of Radovan Karadzic, but I didn't recognise the other voice. So just one voice: Radovan Karadzic's.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Maybe we can put the English translation on the overhead projector so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if I can assist you. You distributed the separate binder for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- for the intercepts to be played in the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The order -- the binding order is out -- is not orderly manner, and the first document is that -- I think this is the first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. It's the second one. We have already played one, and it's actually exactly in the order that they are played. It's now the second document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First document. So the interpreters may be mistaken with the order. You can check with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe you. The problem is, I personally do not have this binder, and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, could you get it during the adjournment? Could you get it during the adjournment, and then at least we'll be speaking from the same sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I actually have it here. The interpreter should have that copy.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have a copy, but it's unmarked, so we're unable to find the exact portion, and we can't translate from the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we can waste any further time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Will the witness be able to identify the second speaker if more is played, do you anticipate, or does he simply not know who this man is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the second man is? Could you identify the second speaker to speak in addition to Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the conversation that I listened to and from the transcript, this one here, and from the information that the other participant in the conversation referred to, it is Vojko Djogo [as interpreted], the president of the Association of the Serbs in Belgrade. Serbs from Bosnia-Herzegovina in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met him on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we simply follow now the transcript on page 2, and you can see it now on the ELMO. There it says: GOJKO DJOGO: Where does he ... where does he mean to start a war in Sarajevo? Is he a madman? RADOVAN KARADZIC: He is. I think that they should be beaten if they start the war. They will be ... they will ... well, they will disappear, that is... GOJKO DJOGO: There will be a lot of blood, but ... RADOVAN KARADZIC: They will disappear, that people will disappear from the face of the earth if they, if they insist now. Their only chance was to accept what we had offered them. It was too much, we did offer them too much. To which people is Mr. Karadzic referring, and what does he mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like -- I would like to direct you now to the page 6. That's the second marked, the second marked part. If it could be put on the ELMO so that I can read it. GJOKO DJOGO: Oh, my God, let them cleanse this down there ... let them, just one night ... here, they killed them 8 people, why didn't they ... 8 people, why didn't they attack Dubrovnik after last night, man!? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Well, yes. And they killed them on Bosnian side. GJOKO DJOGO: First 8 people in Ravno, man. Well, that's ... that Ravno in Popovo? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Of course, on Bosnian side, that is in Bosnia-Herzegovina. GJOKO DJOGO: Well, you know what should be done ... that is good enough reason to raid Dubrovnik tonight. And Mr. Karadzic said: "Yes." To which Ravno are they referring, and to which killing of eight people? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ravno is a place in Herzegovina, on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina near Dubrovnik, and it was there where there was fighting, and some people were killed, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- yes. Thank you. And we now go further, to the next section that is marked. It starts on the same page, and it starts with --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. From the text here, they were killed -- eight people were killed, but I can't say exactly who. I know that there was fighting there, but I don't actually know who it was who was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next -- the next quote: RADOVAN KARADZIC: There isn't. They, they incite the irresponsible MPs to follow that idea, that they have to get a state. They scared them with Serbs, as if Serbs did any harm to anyone. And then they made the commitment that now ... and then this Milos ... this what's-his-name made, Izetbegovic towards Tudjman, and Tudjman towards him, and one encourages the other, you know. Since ... this ... Izetbegovic has promised Tudjman the whole Bosnia, and Tudjman encourages ... and he promises him that the Muslims will rise against the Serbs to fight. GJOKO DJOGO: You just keep on lying them a little more there, do ... you give them milk and honey until this, up there this job has accumulated until they determine, until they were cleansed this terrain in order to ... And then Mr. Karadzic says: RADOVAN KARADZIC: Aha. Well, no. They must know that there are 20.000 armed Serbs around Sarajevo, man. This is not normal, they will, they will disappear! Sarajevo will be a melting pot in which 300.000 Muslims will die. They are not normal. I don't know. I'll have to tell them openly now: people, don't push your fuckin' luck - there are three, four hundred thousand armed Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina. What do you think? In addition, there is the army, technical equipment and all. What do you think you can do, secede like Croatia did? And they do literally go ... yesterday, they told us during these negotiations, I mean at the Assembly session, that the sovereign Bosnia means independent Bosnia, in case that Yugoslavia ends ... Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a conversation about the positions of Alija Izetbegovic and the SDA party and the Bosnian Muslims and the relationship of Karadzic towards them. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there 20.000 armed Serbs around Sarajevo? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many there were, but I do know that the Serbs armed themselves around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Tapuskovic is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic -- I'm sorry. Mr. Tapuskovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we've already cleared this point up, that is that the witness is just there to say whether he recognises the voices and not to say what he thinks somebody thought when he said what he said. I don't think that that is the object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. He can't say what he thinks somebody is thinking. That's for the other person to say. He can, however, give evidence about factual matters about which he knows which arise from what's said on the tape. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We go to the next marked quote. It's on page 8 in the English, and Mr. Radovan Karadzic says there: RADOVAN KARADZIC: We will not force them into anything, but they do not have a way to secede. I think this is clear to the army, to everyone. It will be bloodshed. The army will not, well, use 2 planes but will use 20 in every action ... I go now to another part that is marked. It's on page 10, and there is a reference to Vukovar, and Mr. Djogo says: GJOKO DJOGO: That damned Vukovar, it's a stick in the throat, man! RADOVAN KARADZIC: OK, that is not important. It is under siege. There are just some rats in the holes. However, what is most important is that Bos ... Bosnia is full of soldiers, you know. Was Bosnia at that time full of soldiers, and if so, what kind of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is said here about Vukovar, does that match with your own knowledge of the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know that Vukovar was in an encirclement for several months, encircled by the JNA forces and the armed units under its command or working together with the JNA. Up until the 18th of November, that is, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then on page 14 there is another section where references are made to territories, and Mr. Djogo says. GJOKO DJOGO: Sorry, they should say that is strategic, you know - two or three villages, as well as these do here. Hats off to what they have done in, in ... barbarian act, burn everything - the end of story! Certain territory, the one around the border, has to be cleansed. Do you know to which this refers? Actually, there is also a quote before that where they speak about Dubrovnik. Do you know to which part of the conversation this refers to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the area around Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is cleansing what, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA is taking control of that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic continues in relation to Dubrovnik. He said: RADOVAN KARADZIC: Dubrovnik was never ... never Croatian. GJOKO DJOGO: Eh, to shorten this ... of Dubrovnik ... to end them and exactly there, where they have stopped now, near the little bridge near Cavtat. And a little further down they speak about the Dubrovacka River and everybody should be killed there, and Mr. Karadzic says: RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. And Mr. Djogo says: GJOKO DJOGO: Kill everyone. To whom does this refer? Who should kill everyone, and which region is meant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Tapuskovic's comment is right there. That's for us to determine from what is said in the conversation. The witness can say what he knows of his own knowledge, but this is just a matter of interpretation of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who at that time -- where -- who was in Cavtat securing a region up to Cavtat? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The enemy side. The enemies to the JNA, that is to say the army of the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was at that time the JNA? We're talking of October 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area around Dubrovnik. They were deployed there. Cavtat is right by Dubrovnik. Dubrovacka Rijeka is to the north of Dubrovnik, so that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is all in relation to this intercept, and I would like to turn now to the next intercept. We actually had planned to play a part of it, and I wonder if we should give it another try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which tab are we on? Which tab?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's tab 30, and the witness should have the B/C/S transcript, and on the overhead projector we should put the marked section. For the technical booth, it's track 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think we can -- we can't hear this properly and should not do it. I'm a little bit surprised because the quality was very well during the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, if we cannot hear -- we cannot play the video, how can you confirm the content of the transcript? By the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness actually heard this, these intercepts in the preparation for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear this intercept and could you actually listen to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you assist the translators providing the transcript of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, he listened to the intercept, and at the same time had the transcript, the B/C/S transcript, to check whether it is the text that is spoken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you listen to the intercept, or was it also so disturbed? Can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation was much clearer, much more discernible, when I listened to it the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that the booth haven't got the original. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: They should have the CD that we actually also had, and it was clear, clearly -- you could hear it clearly, and there was no noise in it like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It was actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with this CD. We cannot waste further time on it now. I suggest that during the adjournment, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, you deal with the booth and see what the problem is, and we can return to it in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can play this intercept at a later stage and give it another try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have to also note, the pagination is different between the separate binder and the original binder. The pagination is all different, in a special document also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Pagination is important in all these bundles. The Prosecution should have every bundle paginated, or otherwise we are in total confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will check in the break. We will check on these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have described this pattern of events, and you described the regions in Croatia where you saw this happen. Was this pattern restricted to Croatian territories only or did you see that being repeated elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw, first of all in August 1992, and then later on as well, in the subsequent months and years that followed, that the same thing happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you -- and how -- did you go there, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I passed by that way, I saw that the settlements in which Croats and Muslims had lived before the war were devastated, completely empty and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And through which regions did you pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through Bosanski Novi, Sanski Most, Prijedor, the area around Banja Luka, towards Brcko and Bijeljina, the area around Zvornik, towards Han Pijesak and Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milosevic know what was happening on the ground? Can you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have known his service was present there, and I met the head of his security service down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have to go into private session for the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said you met the head of his security service down there. Whom did you meet, and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic. Jovica Stanisic I met in the area for the first time sometime in May 1991. It was April or May of 1991. And then I met him again in May 1995, together with Franko Simatovic, nicknamed Frenki. Mile Grbic from Bosanski Novi told me that he had firm links and contacts with Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you meet Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic in -- No. I mean, where did you meet Jovica Stanisic in May 1991? What kind of a meeting was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Radovan Karadzic's flat. It was a meeting in Radovan Karadzic's flat, and also present were Milan Martic and Velibor Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Velibor Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the Executive Board of the SDS for Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was Minister of Information for a time and a close associate of Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this meeting? What did you discuss there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, the people who led the conversation were Ostojic, Stanisic, and Karadzic, and they were discussing some maps, where the Serbs were in control and areas where they should establish control, or rather, the SDS, Karadzic's SDS party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were you and Mr. Martic there? Why were you taking part --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Martic told me that Jovica Stanisic had asked us to come. It was my impression that we were just supposed to make "un acte de presence" there in Karadzic's flat. After that, we went to the SDS club in Sarajevo, which means we had dinner, actually. So he just wanted us to be present. That was my impression. We didn't have any great role to play in the conversation at all. We weren't asked, actually, about anything. We weren't asked our opinions. We just passed through Sarajevo and some of the settlements around it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you met Mr. Stanisic in May 1995 in Bosnia. What was the -- what were the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: En route to Vukovar, and an Assembly of the Republic of Srpska Krajina was being held there in May 1995. I was invited to stop by in Bijeljina, to go to the municipality there, and from the municipality, they escorted me to the centre of the security service, or whatever it was called, the CBS in Bijeljina, and that was where Jovica Stanisic was, as well as Franko Simatovic, "Frenki", and Radovan Karadzic. Momcilo Krajisnik was also there. And I was accompanied by Rajko Lazajic, president of the Assembly of the RSK. Where he actually entered the hall, the room itself, I can't remember, but I think he went in together with me. And they had asked for me, because Stanisic and Karadzic had an idea, that is to say, through the social accounting service in Vukovar, the branch in Vukovar, to have fictitious payments paid into an account for military materiel and equipment, for weapons and ammunition which the Republika Srpska had procured in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it discussed which military materiel were received when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. They just spoke about weapons and ammunition. I don't know what ones precisely. But it was a large quantity. I can't remember exactly how much, but quite large. According to my assessments at the time and the insight I had into matters of that kind, there was an inflation in May in Serbia, so there was a large money mass that was discussed. As to the type of weapons, I don't remember them specifying what kind of weapons and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it discussed from where -- you said the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Was it said in which way the weapons were received and from which factories or source?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mentioned Kragujevac or Krusik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kragujevac is in -- is it in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is in control of the factories in Kragujevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a so-called special purpose plant used for military purposes, and it was controlled by the army, that is, the Ministry of Defence; the army of Yugoslavia and the Ministry of Defence, that is, the government of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why were you asked to get involved and make fictitious payments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, the Prime Minister of Srpska Krajina was Borislav Mikelic, and Stanisic was in the Serbian Security Service, and they had a disagreement about the distribution of oil and of petroleum derivatives, and maybe that's why they didn't discuss it with him. He was in charge of such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness will have to make plain what the plan was, because it's not at all clear. What was the plan - just explain it to us so we can understand it - that they were discussing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were discussing -- or rather, they were asking that, through the branch of the public accountancy service in Vukovar on the territory of the Republika Srpska Krajina, a fictitious payment should be made, on paper only, to factories in Serbia producing military equipment, and this equipment was purchased from Serbia by Karadzic, by the authorities of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why couldn't the -- why could Republika Srpska not simply pay for the weapons they had gotten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- well, it couldn't pay because I assume they had no money, and they couldn't make this fictitious payment from Republika Srpska because there were no payments and no transactions between Republika Srpska and Yugoslavia. They had been cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an embargo imposed on Republika Srpska at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia imposed, because of the amounts from the international community, an embargo, but this was only a pretense, and these were ways of actually getting around the embargo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we actually have left a little bit the proofing summary, the order of the proofing summary, in relation to the limited time that I have. We are now talking about paragraph 272 in the proofing summary, the relationship with the Bosnian Serbs, Serbia Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually assist in the way that you were asked to assist, that is, fake payments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was not in charge of this, and secondly, I didn't like this. I didn't see any reason why I should be asked to do this. I was the Minister of External Affairs, and Stanisic had complete control over Vukovar. I didn't go into any explanations, but I said it couldn't be done. And Krajisnik said, "Yes, yes, it can be done. I know. I'm an economist." However, I did nothing in this regard. I simply knew that this would be an inflationary move against Serbia and that we would suffer the consequences for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a disagreement with Mr. Mikelic -- between Mr. Mikelic and Mr. Stanisic in relation to oil. Was the Republika Srpska at that time also supported with oil deliveries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The State Security Service transported secretly over the River Sava petroleum derivatives for the Republic of Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where to where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in this way, distribution of oil from Mirkovci, Eastern Slavonia, which was then processed in the Pancevo refinery near Belgrade, was transported, and I also heard there had been some illegal purchases going against the embargo, imports of oil into Yugoslavia, and then it was distributed from Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the problem with Mr. Mikelic in this regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In regard to the distribution of quantities, what was for Serbia and what was for Republika Srpska Krajina, because Mikelic was authorised to distribute the oil taken from Mirkovci and processed in the Pancevo refinery.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a mistake in the transcript, obviously. There is a reference to -- there is a reference to Mr. Krajisnik, that he said, "Yes, yes, it can be done." I do not think that the witness actually said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who said -- who confirmed that it could be done, this fake payment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Stanisic and Karadzic who asked me to do this. When I said it couldn't be done, Krajisnik said yes. He said he knew it could be done, because he was an economist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. In relation to the matters that you just referred to, that is, the oil deliveries, I would like to put two documents to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're still in private session. Do we need to be in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go now into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to put to the witness two exhibits from Exhibit 352, tab 93 and tab 94. The first document, tab 93, is a document listed under the title "Ministry of Defence of the RSK," and it's dated the 2nd of August, 1994, to The President of the Republics. In this document, there is referred to a dramatic situation in relation to the fuel needed by the army and the limited amount that they actually get.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this document, looking at the stamp and looking at the signature, is this a -- is that how you remembered the stamp and the letterhead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and the content as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This shortage, who decided, actually, who received the deliveries of oil? Who made this decision about the deliveries of the oil that was provided to the RSK and the RS? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovica Stanisic, Mihalj Kertes, and Boro Mikelic. They controlled the flow of oil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because Boro Mikelic told me. Radovan Stojicic "Badza" also told me, and so did people from Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other document that I would like to put to you, it is a petition in relation -- to the president of the RSK and other officials of the RSK, in relation to the state of affairs in the Krajina Petroleum Refining and Sales Enterprise, seated in Mirkovci, and that is dated the 15th of July, 1994, and it's also again about the distribution of petroleum and petroleum products. Can you comment on this document in relation to the letterhead and the contents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it says who received this and what the date was and under what number it was registered, and the signatures are those of people from Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we go in private session for one question?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are listed here as one of the persons who received this document. Did you receive this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I was also told orally about these requests by people from Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these also the people who informed you about the role of Stanisic and Kertes in relation to the oil production there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like to return now to what we discussed about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have -- we did speak about the events that unfolded, and you described the pattern of attacks that occurred and what happened to the non-Serb population in the territories. When you saw the events develop, did you realise what the plan was for the non-Serb population in the regions that were to become part of the joint Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the SAO Krajina, I understood that this was a consequence of the way in which the war was waged rather than part of a plan. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. However, in my view, this -- it was simply that the manner in which the war was waged was the same in all areas, and those were the things that happened. As for the interests of the Serbian people in the SAO Krajina, this went against the interests of the Serbian people in the SAO Krajina. It was a disaster for the people in the SAO Krajina as much as it was for the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you -- when did this pattern start to be -- to become clear to you? Which time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to November 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said up to November. When did it start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. It started even earlier. It started in May 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had said on the first day of your testimony, you actually had mentioned that you believed in the beginning that the Serbs in Croatia were endangered in their position. At that time in May 1991 and up to November 1991, did you still believe that the Serbs in Croatia were endangered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally believed it, up until the moment the JNA joined in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The state -- the state for all Serbs that you mentioned to be the goal, was it ever given up until 1995 or was it pursued further?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea was not given up, but the territory was revised on which the state would be created.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through which events was it revised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many events. President Milosevic and Radovan Karadzic changed their plan. The Serb territories in Croatia were to be given over to Croatian authority, and the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to be divided between the Serbs and the Croats -- rather, between Croatia and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like now to turn to a different issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have to return to this as soon as we have sorted out the intercept problem, because we have several intercepts related to this situation, but I will now move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have mentioned that you met Mr. Milosevic on a lot of occasions, but we have no time to go into all these occasions. We have to discuss just a few of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: First of all, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First in general terms, you said you met him, Mr. Milosevic, about 30 -- around 30 times. When you met him, how did you address him, and how did he address you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I addressed him as Mr. President. He addressed me by my name, my first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that ever change? Did you ever get close?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also saw him together with Mr. Karadzic. How did Mr. Karadzic address Mr. Milosevic, and how did Mr. Milosevic address Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic also addressed him as Mr. President. Milosevic addressed him by his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First name or last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called him Radovan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you meet Mr. Milosevic for the first time and for the last time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I personally met him in October 1990. The last time in August, around the 8th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- when you saw him for the first time in October 1990, what was the topic of the conversation that you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been given the task by the president of the Serb Democratic Party, Mr. Raskovic, who gave me Milosevic's telephone number, to call him and to go and see him and ask him whether he would oppose the idea of the Serb Democratic Party with its seat in Knin but which is also active on the territory of Serbia, whether he would oppose its participating in the elections that had been scheduled to be held in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean you had to ask him for his consent or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, I was to test the ground to see whether he would oppose this. So yes, to see whether he would oppose it or not. I was to get from him his non-opposition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get this non-opposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He said, "Well, in Vojvodina where the SBO has some influence, yes, it could participate."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you met him on this first occasion and on later occasions, did you speak with him about the situation in Croatia and what was happening on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the usual topic of conversation during every visit. I told him of my fears and anxieties as to what would happen to us, the Serbs in Croatia and the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his reaction to those kind of talks when you told him those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we would be protected by the JNA. That's what he kept repeating. "The JNA will protect you." And he said the Serbs had the right to self-determination and to remain in the same state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned a meeting with Mr. Milosevic in which a financial matter in relation to the screw factory was discussed. When you discussed this with Mr. Milosevic, was someone else present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djoko Majstorovic, the administrative secretary of the Main Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We do not have to repeat the financial matter, but on this occasion, was anything else said by Mr. Milosevic, in particular in relation to his position as a party leader?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said he would have to find someone younger and appoint him president of the SBS. I found this rather funny, because he appointed Borislav Jovic to that position, and he wasn't really young.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic is older? Do you mean he's older than Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In terms of years, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason that Mr. Milosevic stepped down as the party president? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the constitution of Serbia, because he was elected president of the Republic, he could not perform any other public functions. Formally, it had to be someone else or, rather, it was really supposed to be someone else, but as far as I could see, it was purely a formality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean he actually stayed in power no matter which function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that you were in Belgrade in January 1991, and did you meet Milosevic in this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the first -- first of all, why were you in Belgrade at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January, I visited Belgrade several times. There was a crisis around the order issued by the Presidency of Yugoslavia about the disarming of paramilitary units in Croatia. On the first occasion, Borivoj Rasuo told me that the JNA was planning a coup d'etat, and he told me how to act if this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you? How --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Are we in closed session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it closed session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said I should obey orders, offer no resistance. I asked whether I would be arrested, and he said no. He just told me not to offer any resistance and to be obedient. On the second occasion, I went there because Mile Grbic and Zika Rakic from Bosanski Novi had told me to go to Colonel Djigurski, who was a colonel of the KOS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have to interrupt because I'm not following this. Borivoj Rasuo. Now, who is he? How does he fit into this matter? I gather it's he who is telling the witness these things. You will have to explore these things, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we have actually already spoken about Boro Rasuo and his position. But just to remind Your Honours...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Boro's position at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, he was an expert advisor in the Marxist Centre of the Central Committee of the League of Communists of Serbia while it existed. In late 1990, he left this centre, and then he became the director of the Yugoslav Institute for Journalism. In the meantime, he had some sort of public post, but I don't remember exactly what. He was close to Mihajlo Markovic, the ideologue of the SPS and various political figures, and in 1994 and 1995, I realised he was also close to Jovica Stanisic. At that time, he became a close friend of mine. He originated from Knin. He often visited Knin. He would transmit information from Belgrade to me. We had a similar background, similar education. He became my political advisor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when was he your political advisor? At the time we are talking about now, that is the end of 1990, was he your advisor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He formally became my advisor later, in the second half of 1991, and a Minister of External Affairs in the government of the SAO Krajina. But at that time, he was informally my advisor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was close to Jovica Stanisic. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April 1994, when talks were held about establishing a government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in Milan Martic's residence in Belgrade, Jovica Stanisic was present. So was Brana Crncevic and other people; Borislav Mikelic. And my proposal was because I was the president of a party that had a large number of MPs in the parliament, that Borivoj Rasuo should -- well, I apologise. First I proposed Lazar Macura as Minister of Information. Martic opposed this. Then I nominated Borivoj Rasuo. Martic opposed this too. And then Jovica nodded his head and said yes, and then Martic said, "Yes. All right." Before that, during the election campaign in Mirkovci, when we were in Mirkovci, Rasuo said that he had talked to Stanic and that I should call him, but I didn't. Later on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt for a moment. I see we've gone beyond the time for an adjournment. No doubt you could look into the tapes and we'll go on then.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- the Prosecution will play the intercepts a little bit later, in a context where they fit better than where we are now. And we are still in private session, and I would like to clarify something with the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly: Boro Rasuo told you in January 1991 that a coup was planned and that you should not resist it? What kind of a coup did he speak about, and who planned that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was saying that the JNA would carry out the coup, and that with respect to Knin and me, as the president of the Knin municipality, he said that they would appoint a governor of the municipality and that I shouldn't resist. So this referred to Croatia. Whether he meant anything more than that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he said "a coup," a coup against the Croatian authorities or against whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against the authorities. There would be a change of government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned the persons Mile Grbic and Zika Rakic. What did they tell you, and who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are two Serbs from Bosanski Novi. In 1990, in August, they brought weapons to Martic in Knin, and in 1991, they also supplied with weapons that they had obtained in Serbia through Jovica Stanisic, and distributed those weapons in SAO Krajina. Zika Rakic was later on Minister of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that Stanisic was involved in this weapons transfer? How do you know that? Did any of these two men tell you about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Grbic told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his relationship with Stanisic? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were close, in business and political terms. He mentioned him regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "he," you refer to Mr. Grbic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to that situation in January 1991, you mentioned the two of them. What did they tell you about the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they had information from the army that the army would intervene in Croatia against the Croatian government, and that I could get more information from Colonel Djigurski, a KOS colonel who was in Zemun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, I'm concerned about the value of the evidence of this sort. These are reports, at best secondhand. Although we allow hearsay, there must be a limit really to what we can admit and the value of these reports. It may be that there is some particular value that you want to rely on, but given the time, I wonder if we need spend too much more on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, what the witness is telling us now explains why he actually ended up in Belgrade and how he met Mr. Milosevic and what Mr. Milosevic then told him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let's perhaps move on to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Djigurski, a KOS member. Did you meet Mr. Djigurski then in January 1991, and did he tell you something about the coup?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a meeting that I had with him in January 1991, but he didn't speak to me about a coup. He inquired about relations within the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on that occasion in January 1992, did you also meet Mr. Milosevic, and how did that come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on two occasions. The first time, somebody told me - I can't remember exactly who in Belgrade - that I should send a request to be received by President Milosevic in connection with the crisis in Croatia and Yugoslavia, and I went. Mile Dakic was with me, the vice-president of the Serbian National Council, and on that occasion we had a conversation. The second time was upon the invitation of President Milosevic, and I came. And he said that he would arrest Martin Spegelj and that I must remain in Belgrade, that I shouldn't be in Knin, so as not to create any problems for the army, that is, the JNA, so that the Croatian government wouldn't arrest me and that would complicate things. And he gave me police protection of the state security and the public security service. So I spent about ten days in Belgrade under that protection, maybe longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This second meeting with Mr. Milosevic, when was that that he told you about the arrest of Spegelj and that you should stay for security reasons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was around the 25th of January, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you met him on that occasion, did you also meet people from the security section and the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milosevic advised me to contact Radmilo Bogdanovic and Jovica Stanisic so that they should provide protection for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they? Were they in that same building as Mr. Milosevic, or where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In another building, in the Knez Milos Street, in the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, the building of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Bogdanovic, what position did he have at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was Minister of Internal Affairs in the government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Stanisic, what was his position then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the officials in the State Security Service of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they provide security then for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Security was provided by the state security, that is, plain-clothes officers, and public security, in the apartment in which I lived, and they also gave me an escort, permanent escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the arrest of Spegelj. Was that at the same time planned when the Spegelj tape that we talked about earlier was actually shown, broadcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, at that time, around the 25th of January, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Belgrade, you said you were there for ten days. Were you allowed to leave Belgrade or actually did you have to stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milosevic told me that I musn't leave Belgrade without his permission. And then, about ten days later, Radmilo Bogdanovic called me and waved his hand and said, "Nothing will come of it. You go back to your people." And that is how I left Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can go into open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radmilo Bogdanovic, was he dismissed at some point in time from his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in March 1991, after the demonstrations staged by the opposition in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Bogdanovic remain in some functions after that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, he had several positions in the Commission for Security of the Assembly in the Assembly of Yugoslavia. He became an official of the SBS and a public servant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he close to Mr. Milosevic? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? Do we need to go into private session for this or can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, how do you know he was close to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in Mr. Milosevic's office about the 20th of March, 1991. Milosevic had called him. And this was during one of my encounters with President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was this meeting on the 20th of March? How did this meeting come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came about because Rastovic, president of the Minicipal Assembly of Donji Lapac and vice-president of the Executive Council of SAO Krajina, wanted us to go to Milosevic - his name was David Rastovic - to see how he would protect us in Krajina. So Rastovic and myself went to see Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you ask of him, of Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that; how was he intending to protect us, because he was always saying the JNA would protect us. And there were the events in Pakrac and other events. And he said, "I have already purchased for you in Hungary 20.000 pieces of weapons." And I said I knew nothing about that. And Rastovic also said that he knew nothing about it. Then we called a third person, Janko Cvetan, who was with us but he had remained in the Moscow Hotel in Belgrade. He was an official of SDS and he was close to Bogoljub Popovic of the SDS, and they were always talking about weapons. So we called him to come to Milosevic's and say whether he knew anything about it. Janko Cvetan came and said that he didn't know anything about it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. When this person, Janko Cvetan, came and spoke about weapons, did he actually openly speak about weapons or did he use other words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody was openly speaking about weapons, Milosevic and Cvetan. That was the issue, weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honours, just for your orientation, we are now in paragraphs 124, 125 of the summary. Would have moved a little bit forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Milosevic's reaction to this conversation about weapons and that you didn't know anything about the weapons he had purchased?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said something like a swear word, and he said, "These people of mine have cheated me or misled me." And then he left to go to the secretary's office. And not long after that, Radmilo Bogdanovic and Jovica Stanisic came, and he asked them, "What about the weapons?" Radmilo Bogdanovic said, "We have already sent 500 pieces to Banija." I said I knew nothing about it. Bogdanovic said, "You don't have to know everything." And Milosevic added, smilingly, "Yes, yes. Milan should know these things." And then Bogdanovic just made a face to the effect, "What are you saying?" Jovica Stanisic didn't say anything. He just had an angry expression on his face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did actually weapons arrive afterwards, or how was this situation solved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons arrived. However, I learnt that the weapons were coming from the warehouses of the Territorial Defence of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Zelenbaba told me, Martic's assistant in the Krajina police. He took me to the village of Raducic, close to Knin, sometime in May 1991. He showed me the weapons, rifles, mortars, and so on. And he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. said that Braco, meaning Mihalj Kertes, was kicking open the doors of the TO warehouses in Serbia. And then in July or the beginning of August in 1991, Mile Grbic told me also that weapons were being brought in from Serbia. He showed me a warehouse with mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, returning to the meeting of the 20th -- of the 20th of March, was anything else discussed except for the weapons? Did you raise other matters in relation to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I complained that I felt that the secretariat of internal affairs of SAO Krajina was not capable of performing these duties, that we needed an expert, somebody -- a professional, somebody who understood these things and who knew how to deal with them, some kind of instructors or legal assistants, and Milosevic said that that would be resolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that matter resolved, and if so, in which way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was resolved, but not in the way that I assumed it would be and expected it would be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had you expected and what actually was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had expected legal assistance, professionals who would work on the organisation of the secretariat of internal affairs in SAO Krajina, that would organise the services within the internal affairs sector. However, instead, officials of the state security arrived, headed by Franko Simatovic, who got the nickname "Frenki" in Knin. And they organised a military camp in Golubic and formed their paramilitary formations, paramilitary army. And they exerted control over the secretariat of internal affairs of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to return to the meetings with Mr. Milosevic and later come back to Frenki. Did you have a meeting with Mr. Milosevic on the 17th of February, 1991, after returning from Geneva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before Geneva and also after Geneva. I think there were two meetings, one before and one after Geneva. I remember when he spoke in negative terms about Jovan Raskovic when he said, "Replace him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you to replace Jovan Raskovic or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he said that to me. And I said that that was impossible, that Jovan Raskovic cannot be replaced, he was a popular tribune. He was a popular leader, a leader of the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the -- you mentioned that you saw him twice, once before Geneva and once after. What actually did you do in Geneva, so that the Judges know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a representative of the world Serbian community at a meeting of the Commission for Human Rights and the Rights of National Minorities. It was a commission of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you meet Mr. Milosevic before and after? Did -- did he ask for that or why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this discussion about Mr. Raskovic, was it before you went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in February. I think it was before, but I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did Mr. Milosevic want Mr. Raskovic to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-061 [Resumed]
